author: latent-seminar page (lowrank.github.io; no named human author)
paraphrase: Outline of the construction: families F_{k,m} with quantum cost about sqrt(m) and randomized cost about m^(2-1/k), built from k-fold Forrelation addresses, winner certificates, probabilistic tournaments and an adaptive direct-product lower bound. It explicitly claims no independent verification, did not audit the Forrelation bound, and found no Lean build or statement match.
reliability_note: Selected-section review of an OpenAI manuscript, self-described as not a verification. Read through a summarising fetch tool, so wording is second-hand.

author: latent-seminar index (lowrank.github.io)
paraphrase: Lists family 284 as nearly quartic quantum query speedups for total Boolean functions, in a reading group on randomized and quantum queries. Notes the manuscripts are produced by an internal OpenAI model and reviews are not full verification.
reliability_note: Index page only; no errors or authors named.

author: Scott Aaronson
paraphrase: Aaronson lists the nearly fourth-power randomized vs quantum separation among OpenAI results, calls it a favourite problem of his, and says it closes the story of the exponent. He says Lean certificates cover only some results and humans are still checking proofs; he does not explain the proof.
reliability_note: Post by a domain expert but not a proof check. Fetched in chunks via a summarising tool; comments 1-349 were scanned for the target names and none of Ben-David, Kothari, Tal, Ambainis, Sinha, Sherstov or Wu appeared in the portion the tool returned.

author: Timothy Chow (comment 235)
paraphrase: Warns that some OpenAI Lean challenge files could allow misleading definitions and that a formal statement may differ from the natural-language one. General to the release, not specific to the quartic result.
reliability_note: Comment number and date from tool summary; not specific to family 284.

author: Scott Aaronson (comment 294)
paraphrase: Says the results need simplifying and re-explaining in human-friendly terms, a task between verification and discovery. General to the release.
reliability_note: Not specific to the quartic result.

author: Tanay Wakhare (comment 337)
paraphrase: Links an open-source GitHub repository with enhanced versions of the OpenAI PDFs. Possibly the community resource the task mentions, but I did not open the repository and its contents are unknown.
reliability_note: Link target not read; unknown whether it covers family 284.

author: Matteo Vitturi (comment 345)
paraphrase: Asks for a short digest of each of the 372 results to help referees. Indicates no per-result digests existed by that date.
reliability_note: General request, not specific to quartic.

author: VibeMathed (aggregator, no named author)
paraphrase: Marks the result Candidate, Unreviewed, and states no independent mathematician has checked it. The page's author read only the abstract, introduction, Theorem 1.1 and the quantum upper bound proposition, and notes the exponent is 4-2/k per fixed k, ruling out any alpha below 4.
reliability_note: Aggregator with partial reading; useful for the 4-2/k statement but not a check.

author: QTransition Labs
paraphrase: Catalogues family 284 as a complexity result with only indirect relevance to post-quantum security, and notes no Lean formalisation is shown. Says claims await independent verification.
reliability_note: Catalogue, no analysis. Only first 100k characters read.

author: Lance Fortnow (catalogue page)
paraphrase: Catalogue entry titled as an optimal quartic separation of randomized and quantum queries, saying the quartic upper bound is tight and cubic bounds are ruled out. No Lean link or verification note in the entry.
reliability_note: Page is a selection of OpenAI manuscripts; whether the description is Fortnow's own was not established. Note the title says optimal, other sources say nearly.

author: Computational Complexity blog (Fortnow, Gasarch)
paraphrase: Posts from 7 Oct to 1 Nov (Open No More, Complexity and Lean, Reading Messy Proofs and others) discuss the OpenAI release generally. The index page listing showed none mentioning the quartic separation.
reliability_note: Only the front page listing was read, not the individual posts; the individual posts may mention it.

author: Mint Research newsletter (Yesterday in AI)
paraphrase: Per a search snippet, says the OpenAI paper claims to refute a conjecture from the 2021 Aaronson, Ben-David, Kothari, Rao, Tal paper, and that the editor did no proof check. I could not locate the passage on the page when fetching the first 100k characters.
reliability_note: Relies on search snippet; unconfirmed on the page itself.

author: Shalev Ben-David and Robin Kothari
paraphrase: Predates the OpenAI result: builds a function with randomized cost about sqrt of certificate complexity and quantum cost about its fourth root. Related background, with no reference to OpenAI.
reliability_note: Different problem (certificate complexity); not a reaction.

author: Andris Ambainis, Janis Iraids, Martins Kokainis
paraphrase: Near-quartic separation between certificate complexity and quantum query complexity for a total function. Related background; the abstract does not mention OpenAI or randomized vs quantum.
reliability_note: Different result; v3 is dated the day of the OpenAI manuscript but shows no link.

author: Samuel Schlesinger (written by a Claude Code subagent)
paraphrase: Merged Lean formalisation of the 2021 upper bound D(f) <= 20736 T^4, the quartic bound that the OpenAI separation would show is tight in exponent. Does not formalise the OpenAI separation or any randomized lower bound.

author: OpenAI
paraphrase: README says about 42 percent of top-line results are formalised and some unformalised results could have issues. Family 284 was not among the families in the reasoning-summary table I saw, and other pages show no Lean for it.
reliability_note: Only README viewed, not CONTENTS.md or formalization.yaml; Lean status for 284 not directly confirmed.
